subject: Simulations for Power Analysis and Effect Sizes

messages.author: 556685e17a412579
messages.subject: Simulations for Power Analysis and Effect Sizes
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am using the paper of Donelly et al. (2022) (https://link.springer.com/article/10.3758/s13428-022-01996-0) for many power analyses.

One of them is an experiment with two groups. Table 3 of the paper gives the code for a multi group power analysis.

However, I am not sure how to determine a small versus a medium effect. In the  case of single group (table 2), the algorithm standardized population parameters. Thus, I can work with standardized betas and have an idea of the effect size.

Yet, in the case of multi groups, this is straightforward. Does anyone have any experience with this topic?

Thanks in advance for your time

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Simulations for Power Analysis and Effect Sizes
parts:
The paper describes how we still considered the standardized beta from the single-group model as the effect size of interest for the multigroup model, so the standardized beta in the multigroup model was in units of marginal SD (i.e., variability of the variable across all groups).  But that is just an idea.  Standardized slopes are not necessarily a clinically meaningful metric, but there aren't general guidelines about what is meaningful.  Practical relevance is very context specific.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
